GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  WP No. 205466 of 2014  ORDER 1.

The petitioners are before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
"(i) Declare that the acquisition proceedings in pursuance of preliminary notification vide Annexure-A in bearing No.LAQ.LMT.SR.3/85-86 dated 28.08.1985 passed by respondent No.3, has lapsed as per Section 24(2) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013, insofar as it pertains to Sy.No.162/3 of Benal village, Tq. Basavanabagewadi, Dist.
Bijapur, in the interest of justice and equity.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
(ii) Issue any other order, direction or writ as this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the facts and circumstances of the case as stated above with costs in the interest of justice and equity."
2.

The sole ground on which the above Writ Petition is filed is that a portion of the land belonging to the petitioners has not been taken possession of by respondent No.3 for and on behalf of beneficiary- respondent No.4 and it is on that basis that, provisions of Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 has been invoked to contend that though compensation is paid, possession having not been taken, acquisition is deemed to have been lapsed.

3. The said ground is no longer available for the petitioners to raise in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Indore Development Authority vs. Manohar Lal and Others reported in (2020)8 SCC 129 more particularly, paragraphs- 164 to 166 which are extracted hereunder:
"164.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority vs. Manohar Lal and Others reported in (2020)8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After considering the various suggestions of the State Government, the Committee made some recommendations, which are extracted hereunder:
"16.5

The Committee note that Clause 24 of the Bill provides that land acquisition cases/process shall be invalid on enactment of the new Act in cases where Collector has not given award or possession of the land has not been taken before the commencement of the proposed legislation.

Some of the representatives of the industry and also the Ministries like Railways and Urban Development submitted before the Committee that land acquisition proceedings already initiated under the Nabis S/O Rajesa Pattalgi By Lrs I And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2703868/
3 existing Land Acquisition Act, 1894 should not lapse as it would lead to time and cost overrun in many infrastructural projects.

entities.text: Nabis S/O Rajesa Pattalgi By Lrs I And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in such cases land compensation and R&R benefits could be allowed as per the provisions of LARR Bill.

The Committee would like the Government to re- examine the issue and incorporate necessary provisions in the Rules to be framed under the new Act with a view to ensuring that the land owners/farmers/affected families get enhanced compensation and R & R package under the provisions of the LARR Bill, 2011 and at the same time,
the pace of implementation of infrastructural projects is not adversely impacted."

165. Debates in the Lok Sabha on 29.8.2013, were referred to during the hearings, to cite various reasons given in respect of the question why effect should be given retrospectively in cases where acquisition has not been completed.

Shri Jairam Ramesh, Minister concerned at the relevant time,
replied to debate about the retrospective part with respect to Section 24 thus:
"...
The Hon'ble Member has also raised question about retrospective clause.
This is about section 24 under which it has been provided that if the award has not been passed under the previous law than the new law will be applicable.
Secondly, if the award has been passed and no compensation has been given and no physical possession has been taken the new law will be applicable.
The third situation where this clause will be applicable is when award has been passed but farmer has not been given more than 50 per cent compensation which will entail enforcement of this law.
The Hon'ble Member and several others have raised this apprehension that this Act will ultimately give vast powers to the bureaucracy.
In regard to this apprehension I would like to say that we have fixed time-limit at every level of the procedure and I hope that the States will adhere to these timelines."
166. It is clear that while replying to the debate, the Minister concerned has stated that there would be lapse only if in case possession has not been taken and compensation has not been paid.
The emphasis right from the beginning was on possession.

Thus, from the perusal of debate too, it is apparent that the word "or" had been understood as "and"."
4.
A perusal of the same would indicate that twin tests have to be satisfied, inasmuch as, both possession should not have been taken and compensation should not have been paid.
In the present case, admittedly, compensation has already been paid.
Twin tests having not been satisfied, the petition would not be maintainable.
5. As such, for the aforesaid reasons and being bound by the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Indore Development Authority (supra), the petition stands dismissed.
